title: DSN subcommands BIND PACKAGE (MEMBER) and BIND PLAN (PKLIST) under IKJEFT01, each continued with a hyphen
shapes: BDLD jcl/BDLDUT5.jcl BND040: EXEC PGM=IKJEFT01, DBRMLIB DD DSN=PROD.BDLD.DBRMLIB, SYSTSIN holds DSN SYSTEM(DB2P), BIND PACKAGE(BDLDCOLL) MEMBER(BDLDDB2) - ACTION(REPLACE), BIND PLAN(BDLDPLN) PKLIST(BDLDCOLL.*) - ACTION(REPLACE), END
asserts: The SYSTSIN stream holds four jcl_utility_cards facts with utility IKJEFT01, dd SYSTSIN: verbs DSN, BIND, BIND and END. Each BIND is one fact with its continuation hyphen dropped and its two lines joined: operands 'PACKAGE(BDLDCOLL) MEMBER(BDLDDB2) ACTION(REPLACE)' and 'PLAN(BDLDPLN) PKLIST(BDLDCOLL.*) ACTION(REPLACE)'. There is no RUN subcommand, so no RUN PROGRAM call_sites fact and no program edge: MEMBER(BDLDDB2) names a DBRM, which the BIND PACKAGE turns into a package, it does not call the COBOL program BDLDDB2 that the DBRM came from. BDLDCOLL.* is a collection and package-id pattern, not a dataset. DBRMLIB is an ordinary jcl_dds and jcl_datasets fact on PROD.BDLD.DBRMLIB.

citations.quote: The DSN subcommand BIND PACKAGE builds an application package.

citations.section: Chapter 9. BIND PACKAGE subcommand (DSN), Example: Replacing a version of a package

citations.quote: Specifies the name of a partitioned data set member or zFS file that contains a DBRM.
Search only the libraries described by the DBRMLIB DD statement
The DSN subcommand BIND PLAN builds an application plan.
The PKLIST option determines the packages to include in a package list.
The object replaces an existing one with the same identifier, and a new entry replaces the old one in the catalog table SYSPLAN or SYSPACKAGE.
